observations: body L1-L15: the end of an-Naysābūrī's description of the seas, begun on p. XXII; each line opens with a guillemet. The omissions are marked by five spaced dots (L5, L9, L21) and by three at the head of the quotation of L23.

body L5, L7, L14, L21: the Arabic words are the readings of the Cairo edition, set inside the Latin parentheses as printed: «طراترون» (for Ṭarābazūn), «البكون» (for Ābaskūn), «سريرة» (for Sarbozah: two dots under the yā’, no dot on either rā’) and «الجبائى» (for al-Ǵayhānī: the dots under the jīm and the bā’, the hamza on its seat, the final yā’ without dots).
body L6, L20: «Ǵīlān» and «al-Ǵayhānī» have the acute above the G.
body L7: a speck at the foot of the line between «edit.» and the Arabic word is not transcribed.
body L3, L10: the g of «regionibus» is printed slightly raised; a dot above the u of «quarum» is a speck.

body L9-L12, L32: several t's print without their cross-stroke, like an l («citer», «extremo», «vocata», «praedita», «texte»); the e of «de» (L32) prints broken. They are transcribed as the words read.
body L16, L18: paragraphs beginning inside the entry.
body L18-L20: «al-Kharaqī» (L18), «Fakhr ad-dīn ar-Rāzī» and «al-Ǵayhānī» are letter-spaced; «al-Kharaqī» in L22 is not.
body L19: the year 606 of the Hijra began on 5 July 1209 (6 July in the civil reckoning) and ended in June 1210; «1209» is the year of its beginning.
notes_left L2: the year 310 of the Hijra ran from 30 April 922 to 20 April 923, as printed («922-923»).
body L20: the hyphen of «1308-10» is short (2.0 pt).
body L25-L26: «‘Aden» has the sign of the ‘ayn; «al-khalīǵ» has the acute above the g, «al-akhḍar» the dot under the d.

body L28-L39: the entry on pp. 175-177, «175–177» bold at the margin with a long dash (5.9 pt). De Goeje's French letter follows, each line opening with a guillemet. «de Goeje», «Qodāmah» (L28, L31, L35) and «Ibn Rosteh» (L33, L39) are letter-spaced.

body L29, L32-L34, L39: the Arabic words are set right to left inside the French lines as printed: «المتصل بالبحر الاخضر» (L29); «والموضع» at the right end of L32, after five spaced dots, and «الاخضر» at the head of L33, after the guillemet; «وهذا البحر الاخضر» before the comma and «مائتا ميـل» at the right end of L34; «البحر الاخير» (L39). «الا» at the head of «الاخضر» and «الاخير» is printed as one sort: the strokes of the lām-alif cross like an X under a forked top, and no separate alif of the article stands before it; the elongated join of «ميـل» is transcribed with a tatweel.
body L33: «on pris» is printed so, for «ont pris»; transcribed as printed.
body L34: no stop follows «مائتا ميـل», at the end of the sentence. A small tick after «avant» (0.6 by 1.3 pt, at half the height of the letters) is a speck.
body L38: the hyphen of «au-dessus» is printed as a round dot (1.2 pt) at the height of a hyphen.
body: the dashes measure 9.8-10.2 pt (L5, L9); the signs = are printed long (9.6-10.8 pt).

notes_left L1-L7, notes_right L1-L7: three notes in two columns with a thin rule between them; note 2 runs from the left column into the right. «Marquart», «Abū ’l-fidā’», «al-Qazwīnī», «ad-Dimashqī», «Frähn» and «al-Kharaqī» (divided «al-Kha-», «raqī») are letter-spaced. Note 1 ends with the closing parenthesis, without a stop.
notes_left L5: «ورتك» is the reading of the edition (p. 78), with the two dots of the tā’; the tails of its wāw and rā’ reach into the line below.
notes_left L6-L7: «ut» and «ram» print heavily inked, like bold; they are roman. The t of «t. I» prints broken. The hyphen of «al-Qazwīnī» is printed as a round dot, like the hyphen of body L38.
notes_right L3: the hyphen at the end of the line («Peters-») is short (1.6 pt).
notes_right L7: note 3 ends with a comma. A dot under the foot of the q of «raqī» is a speck.
source_authority: Controlling master page image. Embedded text is not the authority for a reading.
transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
